stories.title: Patching the edge starts with knowing which evidence changed
stories.summary: A practical vulnerability brief shows how teams can separate severity, exploitation evidence, and deployment exposure before opening an emergency change.
stories.why_it_matters: A critical score alone does not tell an engineer whether the vulnerable component is deployed, reachable, or already targeted.
stories.action: Confirm the deployed component and version, review vendor guidance, then prioritize reachable systems with exploitation evidence.
body: This fixture brief demonstrates the publication format using a historic vulnerability. It is not a current alert.
Start with inventory and reachability. Preserve the source and observation date for each decision-relevant fact.

stories.title: Agent tool boundaries belong in the architecture, not only in the prompt
stories.summary: A design note for constraining coding-agent actions with scoped credentials and observable tool calls.
stories.why_it_matters: Prompt instructions cannot enforce privileges outside the model.
stories.action: Inventory tool capabilities and bind credentials to the narrowest operation and environment.
body: Treat every agent tool as a capability boundary. The shell, package manager, browser, and source-control client each need explicit constraints.
Useful telemetry records intent, authorization, command, result, and the identity that approved the action.
stories.author: Pankaj Mouriya

stories.title: Signed builds are useful only when verification is part of deployment
stories.summary: Provenance becomes a control when deployment verifies the expected builder, source, and workflow.
stories.why_it_matters: Generating attestations without enforcing them leaves the trust decision unchanged.
stories.action: Define the allowed builder identity and verify provenance before promotion.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: Admission policies need an exception path engineers can audit
stories.summary: A policy rollout pattern pairs blocking rules with time-bound, attributed exceptions.
stories.why_it_matters: Permanent bypasses turn a useful guardrail into documentation.
stories.action: Require owners, expiry, and review evidence for every admission exception.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: Authorization review should start from objects and relationships
stories.summary: A review method maps actors, objects, and allowed relationships before testing endpoints.
stories.why_it_matters: Endpoint-only checklists miss cross-tenant object access.
stories.action: Write object-level authorization invariants and test them across tenant boundaries.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: EPSS is a probability estimate, not a patching deadline
stories.summary: Use EPSS alongside exposure, business context, and exploitation evidence.
stories.why_it_matters: A single percentile can hide the difference between probability and consequence.
stories.action: Record the EPSS model date and combine it with environment-specific exposure.
body: EPSS estimates exploitation probability over a defined horizon. It does not measure asset impact.

stories.title: A leaked token is an incident until revocation and scope are verified
stories.summary: A response sequence covers revocation, audit review, dependent credentials, and recovery evidence.
stories.why_it_matters: Deleting the visible string does not invalidate the credential or undo access.
stories.action: Revoke first, enumerate use, rotate dependent secrets, and preserve the timeline.
body: This is a synthetic incident used to test a structured response layout.

stories.title: Tool watch: a small runtime observer for process and network context
stories.summary: A synthetic open-source tool profile demonstrates how TSD evaluates operational fit.
stories.why_it_matters: Teams need deployment and trust context, not a list of features.
stories.action: Test in an isolated environment and review collection boundaries before adoption.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: Research notes should separate demonstrated results from editorial interpretation
stories.summary: A compact template keeps the original finding distinct from its architecture implications.
stories.why_it_matters: Readers should see where evidence ends and commentary begins.
stories.action: Link the primary work and label every inferred implication.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: Short-lived cloud credentials still need a clear issuer and audience
stories.summary: Credential lifetime helps, but confused-deputy risks remain when trust conditions are broad.
stories.why_it_matters: A short token can still be used against the wrong resource.
stories.action: Constrain issuer, subject, audience, repository, and environment claims.
body: This is a synthetic advisory for layout testing.

stories.title: Package maintainer tokens should not share the blast radius of a workstation
stories.summary: A publishing pattern isolates release credentials and requires provenance for new versions.
stories.why_it_matters: A compromised developer session can otherwise become a registry compromise.
stories.action: Move publishing to protected workflows and remove long-lived local release tokens.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: A fixed version needs a vendor source, not a guess from the latest release
stories.summary: Version claims remain unknown until an authoritative advisory defines the repaired range.
stories.why_it_matters: Latest does not always mean fixed, supported, or compatible.
stories.action: Preserve advisory ranges and display unknown when no authoritative fix is published.
body: This is a synthetic scenario for layout testing.

stories.title: A critical CVE count is not a vulnerability-management outcome
stories.summary: Measure reachable exposure, remediation progress, and exception age instead of raw totals.
stories.why_it_matters: Counts reward inventory changes and ignore exploitability and ownership.
stories.action: Track decision-ready exposure and aged exceptions by accountable service.
body: The useful unit is a decision: mitigate, accept with evidence, or prove the component is not affected.
stories.author: Pankaj Mouriya

stories.title: Incident diagram: from a package install to a cloud API call
stories.summary: A synthetic attack path highlights credential access and API telemetry opportunities.
stories.why_it_matters: Detection coverage improves when teams map the transitions, not only the initial package.
stories.action: Correlate package execution, process lineage, credential reads, and outbound API calls.
body: This is a synthetic incident for layout testing.

stories.title: From the editor: evidence before prose
stories.summary: The publication separates sourced facts, generated summaries, and editorial judgment.
stories.why_it_matters: Security decisions should remain traceable to evidence.
stories.action: Use the source links and dates; treat summaries as a path into the evidence.
body: The newspaper format is useful because it makes priority visible. Provenance keeps that priority accountable.
stories.author: Pankaj Mouriya
